summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives arbitrary shell/file/process execution on installer host
details: The vanexa-agent daemon opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Workers relay at wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev/ws/daemon/<sessionId>. On `task_request` messages, it instantiates an AgentLoop whose tool registry includes `terminal_exec` (spawns `/bin/bash -c <command>`), `fs_write`, `fs_delete`, `process_kill`, and `browser_act` — so messages received from the relay drive arbitrary shell commands, filesystem writes/deletes, and process control on the installer's host. A `config_update` message from the same relay can set `sandbox.grantAllAccess = true` and rewrite `workspacePaths` live, expanding the agent's filesystem authority without local user action. The relay hostname sits on a personal-looking `hanazaki542.workers.dev` subaccount, unrelated to any vanexa-branded infrastructure, and configuration-load code silently rewrites the older `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` value to this destination. Whoever controls that relay holds a remote shell into every host running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
